name: Chips and Compute
summary: The current shelf now connects semiconductor and AI infrastructure to a Northern Virginia compute corridor where regional demand must pass through large-load tariffs, transmission, local standards, air permits, water service, construction, and energization.
watch_questions: Can fabs and data centers secure enough power, water, labor, and capital?
Which chip supply-chain moves change local equilibria?
Which named data-center loads progress from forecast and permit records into customer service, construction, energization, and measured operation?
Which Phase 56O priority portfolio next supplies action-level implementation evidence rather than aggregate movement?
Which modeled or stated benefit later becomes independently attributed and realized without becoming an agency ranking?
Which BEAD entities progress from signed agreements into constructed, tested, adopted, and closed-out service?
